newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS-ISS closes troubled U.S. chapter.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ISS closes troubled U.S. chapter.

text.p: Danish cleaning group ISS closed the book Tuesday on what it said was its worst year ever and looked forward to better times ahead following the sale of its troubled U.S. unit ISS Inc.

Battered by losses allowed to mount unseen because of false accounting by its U.S. albatross, the group reported a 1.86 billion crown net loss for 1996, compared to a revised 20 million crown profit the year before.
"In 1996 the ISS group experienced its most difficult year, in spite of highly satisfactory results from its two large divisions, ISS Scandinavia and ISS Europe," the group annual report said.
"The problems at ISS Inc., with accounting irregularities, understatement of self-insurance provisions, writedown of goodwill etc., led to a group net loss of 1.856 million."
But the group said that with last December's sale of ISS Inc. to Canada's Aaxis Ltd ending its liabilities it looked forward to improved profitablity and a more stable share price in 1997.

"Following the divestment of ISS Inc., ISS has reduced turnover, but profitablity and key figures in all areas have improved substantially and the uncertainty arising from ISS Inc. that has caused substantial fluctuations in ISS' share price during the past year has been eliminated," its 1996 report said.
"After the sale of ISS Inc. the ISS group has a higher organic growth rate, a better profit margin, improved free cash flow, lower debtor days and an improved equity ratio," it said.
"Organic growth will be supplemented by strategic acquisitions, for which there are many potential candidates."
1996 group turnover was up by a billion crowns, to 15.396 from 1995's 14.391, and operating profit rose to 619 million crowns in 1996 from 572 million the year before.
Analysts' average forecasts were for turnover of 15.750 billion crowns, with operating profit of 630 million.
The market looked past the bottom-line loss to the underlying figures and bullish outlook.
The group's share had traded up to 183.55 crowns by midday, from Monday's closing 178.2 and industry analysts saw further strengthening ahead.
"Given generally stable conditions (the share) will outperform from now on. I believe that many people will come to see ISS with new eyes," an analyst said.
